name: Royal Palace and Museum of Foumban (Bamum kingdom)
subtitle: The royal palace in Foumban was built during the reign of King Njoya, who also opened royal treasures to the wider community.

facts.label: Palace
facts.value: Njoya's reign (1889-1933) saw the construction of a magnificent palace in Foumban.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Njoya decided to open the royal treasures to the wider community, breaking with a tradition of exclusivity tied to specific ceremonies.

facts.label: Museum move
facts.value: The museum was originally in the royal palace and was relocated to a new building under King Ibrahim Mbombo Njoya.

facts.label: Collection
facts.value: The African Mirror reports that the king built a royal museum housing over 3,000 artifacts.

facts.label: Collection
facts.value: AFP reports the Museum of the Bamoun Kings contains 12,500 pieces, including weapons, pipes and musical instruments, only a few previously shown in the palace (counts differ between sources).

facts.label: Why a new building
facts.value: Construction of the new museum was launched in 2013 because the palace rooms were too cramped.

facts.label: Living heritage
facts.value: The Nguon, a set of Bamoun rituals celebrated in an annual festival, joined UNESCO's Intangible Heritage list months before the museum opened (April 2024).

parts.text: The royal palace in Foumban was built during the reign of King Njoya, who also opened royal treasures to the wider community. The museum, first in the palace, was moved to a new building under King Ibrahim Mbombo Njoya; reports on its holdings range from over 3,000 to 12,500 pieces.
